cards.explanation: The answer is that moth and rust destroy it and thieves steal it. Jesus says treasure on earth is where "…moth and rust destroy, and where thieves break in and steal." Think of a cookie jar left on an open counter. A thief walks in, the cookies are gone, and I promise it wasn't a moth.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also." So your heart follows your treasure. I'd say that's worth checking, because I once watched a baker's eyes follow a fresh tray across a whole room.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "But if your eyes are bad, your whole body will be full of darkness." Not a patch of it. The whole body, the same "whole body" He used for the light in the verse before.

The answer is that he'll love one and hate the other. Jesus says, "Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other." You can't split down the middle, friends. One master ends up with your heart.
The answer is money. Jesus says, "You cannot serve both God and money." He's been talking about treasure, and now He names the rival master. Notice He says both, and you can't have it that way.

The answer is that life and body are worth more than food and clothes. Jesus asks, "Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothes?" He's saying you matter more than the things you're worrying over.

The answer is that your heavenly Father feeds them. Jesus says the birds "…do not sow or reap or gather into barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them." The birds aren't doing the farm work. Your heavenly Father is the one feeding them.

The answer is False. Jesus asks, "Are you not much more valuable than they?" He's saying the opposite of the claim. If the Father feeds the birds, you can count on Him for what you need, because you're worth much more.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "…not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these." Solomon, the king of Israel, had more riches than any king on earth (1 Kings 10:23). A lily still beat his wardrobe.

The answer is that He will much more clothe you. Jesus says, "If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, will He not much more clothe you…" If He dresses grass, friends, He'll dress you.

The answer is need. Jesus says the Gentiles, people outside Israel, strive after these things, "…and your heavenly Father knows that you need them." He isn't brushing off food, drink and clothes. He says your Father knows you need them.

The answer is the kingdom of God and His righteousness. Jesus says, "But seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness…" He's just said not to worry about food, drink and clothes, and that the Gentiles strive after them. Now He tells them what to seek first.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "But seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things will be added unto you." The "things" are the food, drink and clothes He's been talking about. He puts the kingdom first and the rest follows.
The answer is trouble. Jesus says, "Today has enough trouble of its own." Each day brings its own load. You don't have to carry tomorrow's too, friends.
